voyage.name: People's Square
voyage.content: What was once the horse-racing track on the edge of the British district is now a large and busy downtown park. The old track's clubhouse now houses a museum and a fine restaurant. Under the square at the edge of the park is a metro station that is one of the hubs of the Shanghai system and one of the busiest subway stations on Earth; lines , and meet there. Nearby are several large high-end malls and department stor

voyage.name: The Bund and the International Settlement
voyage.content: The International Settlement was built North and West of the Old City, starting in the 1840s. In colonial-period Western books, "Shanghai" means that settlement. The Bund’s waterfront complex gathers early 20th-century buildings in Neoclassical, Art Deco, Gothic and other European styles, which once hosted foreign banks, consulates and trading companies.

voyage.name: Shikumen Buildings
voyage.content: Shikumen are unique Shanghai lane houses that blend Western terrace structures with traditional Jiangnan courtyard layouts, marked by their distinctive stone-framed gateways. For shikumen buildings, visit: * Xintiandi, an area of old shikumen houses in the former French Concession, redeveloped with shopping malls, trendy bars and restaurants, and a lot of tourism. * Tianzifang, another area of shikumen housing that h

voyage.name: Garden Villas
voyage.content: Garden villas in the former French Concession were high-end residences built mainly in the 1920s–1940s, featuring spacious plans, private gardens and modern domestic facilities. Many of these well-preserved properties are former homes of famous historical figures. Key sites are found on Wukang Road, Hengshan Road, and within the Sinan Mansions.

voyage.name: Huju
voyage.content: Shanghai Opera is a national intangible cultural heritage and the most representative local opera of Shanghai. It originated from the folk songs and ditties sung by farmers on both sides of the Huangpu River in the late 19th century, and gradually developed into a formal opera as Shanghai grew into a modern city. Different from grand classical Chinese operas, Huju Opera focuses on the daily lives of ordinary Shanghai

voyage.name: Shanghai-style Pingtan
voyage.content: Pingtan is a traditional narrative singing art that spread from Suzhou in the mid-19th century. It is a combination of "Pinghua" (storytelling without singing) and "Tanci" (storytelling with singing). Usually, one or two artists perform on stage, accompanied by traditional Chinese musical instruments: the pipa (a four-stringed lute) and the sanxian (a three-stringed lute). Artists tell classic Chinese folk tales, his

voyage.name: China Odyssey Tours
voyage.content: Tours of the city, for couples and families.

voyage.name: Shanghai Pub Crawl
voyage.content: In addition to a plethora of watering holes ranging from bars, lounges, dives and world-class clubs, there is a pub crawl that arranges transportation to various popular venues. For non-Mandarin speakers or those in town for just a few days, this service takes the guesswork out of finding the hippest, most interesting spots that bustle with expatriates and locals.

voyage.name: Tianchan Beijing Opera Center and Yifu Theater
voyage.content: Beijing Opera or jīngjù (京剧) can be seen in the opera house on Fuzhou Lu 701, on the first corner on your right if you walk down Fuzhou Lu coming from Renmin Square. Chinese opera is very different from its Western counterpart, and you may want to listen to a sample to decide if you'll survive for three hours. Some operas include acrobatic stunts or martial arts displays (Jackie Chan was trained in Chinese opera), ot

voyage.name: Power Station of Art
voyage.price: Free except for special exhibitions. In 2016, combination ticket for the two special exhibitions was ¥60, ¥20 with a student card
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-19:00 (last entry at 18:00), open on all national holidays
voyage.content: Locating on the Huangpu River, this place used to be a power plant and a pavilion for Expo 2010, now the first state-run contemporary art museum in China. It also holds the Shanghai Biennale of contemporary art. You can see the industrial relic of the power plant and the contemporary artworks as well.

voyage.name: Holy Trinity Church (Anglican)
voyage.content: On the east side of People's Square in the old British district.

voyage.name: Fuyou Road Mosque
voyage.content: The mosque traced its origin from 1870 during Tongzhi Emperor of Qing Dynasty. It then underwent renovation in 1897, 1905, 1936 and 1979 to what it is today.

voyage.name: Yuyuan Garden
voyage.address: 279 Yu Yuan Lao Jie, 四牌楼
voyage.content: Beautiful traditional Chinese garden in the heart of Shanghai, next to the City God Temple.

voyage.name: Customs House
voyage.content: An eight-storey building on the Bund featuring a highly visible clocktower nicknamed "Big Ching". Built in 1927, it is seen as one of the symbols of the Bund.

voyage.name: HSBC Building
voyage.content: The grandest building on the Bund is now home to the Pudong Development Bank.

voyage.name: Huangpu Park
voyage.content: At the northern tip of the Bund, was the legendary home of the "No dogs or Chinese" sign — which in fact never existed, although Chinese not accompanied by foreigners were indeed banned until 1928. The Bund Historical Museum located here is also worth a quick visit.

voyage.name: Shanghai Gallery of Art
voyage.address: No. 3, Zhong Shan Dong Yi Road

voyage.name: People's Park
voyage.content: Entry into People's Park on the north half of the square is free, but all attractions listed below are on the edges of the park, not inside.

voyage.name: Shanghai Grand Opera Palace
voyage.content: The Opera Palace is often listed as one of the ten best opera houses in the world. Performances are normally "classic" Western-style opera.

voyage.name: Shanghai Museum
voyage.hours: Daily 09:00-17:00, all year round (last admission at 16:00)
voyage.content: The museum has a huge collection of ancient Chinese antiques, including bronze, ceramics, calligraphy works, painting, jades and sculptures. The Gallery of Ancient Bronze on the first floor is particularly impressive, containing some of the best antiques in China. The exterior evokes a bronze urn, which is appropriate since the museum holds the world's greatest collection of Chinese bronzes. The collection is well-pr

voyage.name: Moca Shanghai
voyage.content: An art gallery by the park.

voyage.name: Shanghai Urban Planning Exhibition Center
voyage.price: ¥30 for adults, ¥15 for students and children
voyage.content: More interesting than you'd expect given its name, this museum documents the history of Shanghai and attempts to chart its future, with changing exhibits on the first two floors and a permanent exhibition on the rest. Many historic pictures from the 19th century introduce still-existing historic places. There is a heavy focus on eco-friendly satellite cities with spacious public centres and loads of greenery. Particu

voyage.name: Shanghai History Museum
voyage.alt: Former club house of the Shanghai Race Club
voyage.content: The Race Club building (1934) has an imposing, 10-storey tall tower which was long a landmark of central Shanghai. The clubhouse's exterior has a neo-classical structure, with eclectic details. Read more on Wikipedia about the Shanghai Race Club. - The museum's large collections focus on the approximately a hundred years in the history of Shanghai from the opening of the port in 1843 to the communist take-over in 194

voyage.name: Huangpu River cruise
voyage.content: At the Bund's southern ferry port with the following: One hour, two-hour and three-hour cruises on the Huangpu. There is a large number of ticket offices and the prices differ slightly.

voyage.name: Huangpu River ferry
voyage.content: For those on a budget or short on time, you can take the ferry across to Pudong. This takes about 15 min and costs ¥2. One of the wharves is located at the Jinling East Road Zhongshan East 2nd Road crossing, as our map shows. Buy the plastic coin or use your metro card. The ferry will drop you in Pudong at the end of Dongchang Road. The best experience is to walk from there, but you can take line 1, which is a red bu

voyage.name: Bund "Sightseeing" Tunnel
voyage.content: A slow-moving tram, through a comically low-tech tunnel with bizarre commentary in English and Chinese. It is marketed as a Sightseeing Tunnel, however there are no sights other than 80s-era rope lights, lasers and some inflatables that look as though they belong in a car dealership. It is a rather surreal experience. This is the fastest way of crossing between the Bund in Puxi and the Pearl TV Tower in Pudong but al

voyage.name: Nanjing Road
voyage.content: It is certainly Shanghai's best-known shopping street, and probably China's. At around a million shoppers a day, it is also one of the world's busiest. It has been busy for generations; Amy Tan's novel The Kitchen God's Wife mentions a figure of 100,000 visitors a day in the 1940s. Nanjing Road starts on the riverside at The Bund and goes about 6 km west from there to Jing'an Temple. It continues beyond the temple, g

voyage.name: 3 on the Bund
voyage.content: Houses the nation's flagship Armani store as well as several critically-acclaimed restaurants.

voyage.name: Suzhou Cobblers
voyage.alt: 上海市黄浦区福州路17号
voyage.content: Beautiful hand-embroidered, Chinese-style silk shoes, slippers, handbags and accessories. A rare combination of historic and modern Shanghai styles.

voyage.name: Da Niang Shui Jiao
voyage.address: East Nanjing Rd. (南京东路 "nanjing dong lu")
voyage.content: Part of a chain of dumpling (饺子 "jiaozi") restaurants around the country. Think of it like the McDonalds of Chinese dumplings. Some of the cheapest food on the Nanjing Rd. pedestrian mall, but be prepared with either a phrase book or a Chinese friend. Dumplings are ordered in "fen". "san fen" (三分) is three fen, a normal-sized plate. To order dumplings: number + "fen" + filling (pork, vegetable, etc.) Soup is also ava

voyage.name: Kebabs on the Grille
voyage.content: Indian cuisine with a new concept of grille on the table.

voyage.name: City Bull Steak House and Bar
voyage.address: 300 Nanjing Rd. at Henan Rd. 2nd floor.
voyage.content: Close to the Bund, great views of the Pearl Tower from the second floor location. Food is reasonably priced and caters to Western palates.

voyage.name: Aunt Jia's Leshan Style Cross-Cut Beef Shanks
voyage.content: Very popular hot pot, with some great other meat and veggie dishes. The "glutinous rice dessert" is delicious.

voyage.name: M on the Bund
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 11:30AM-2:30PM, 6PM-10:30PM daily, Sat Sun brunch 11:30AM-3PM, Sun tea 3:30PM-5:30PM
voyage.content: Open for over a decade, Shanghai's original "new" western restaurant. Attention to detail is given to freshness, quality and presentation. There is an excellent selection of wines to complement your meal and the desserts are extremely tempting. Miele considers it one of the best restaurants in Asia. Also has magnificent views of Pudong from the 7th floor on the waterfront.

voyage.name: Roof 325
voyage.content: The location is atop the colonial-era racetrack clubhouse. The racetrack has now become People's Park and the clubhouse has been restored as the Shanghai Art Museum. The menu offers gastronomical global cuisine with French influence. The views from the glass-encased rooftop and garden terrace are spectacular.

voyage.name: Jamaica Blue
voyage.content: Part of an Australia-based chain with several locations in Shanghai and others around China and the Pacific Rim. Coffee and Western food of good quality, and a range of beers. Patio. Prices are on the high side by Chinese standards, but competitive with other Western restaurants.

voyage.name: Bar Rouge
voyage.content: A magnificent dance club and bar with a terrace on the 7th floor, overlooking the Huangpu River. If you order their signature drink (Bar Rouge), they set the bar alight.

voyage.name: Captain's Bar
voyage.address: 37 Fuzhou Lu, near Sichuan Zhong Lu 福州路37号， 近四川中路
voyage.content: A cheaper bar near the Bund, on the roof of Captain's Hostel. Low-key but welcoming atmosphere, popular with backpackers and visitors to Shanghai, Captain's caters to a younger, less pretentious crowd — a rarity in the district (Cheap mochito for ¥50).

voyage.name: Captain Hostel
voyage.content: Average rooms (which have seen better days), cheap dorms, unbeatable location. Rooms are not clean, some smoky. There is a fantastic rooftop bar directly facing the Bund and the river. You should be aware that while the Bund is swarming with tourists by day, affordable nightlife is sorely lacking in the surrounding area. A taxi ride to the more happening French Concession area is about ¥20.

voyage.name: Hiker Youth Hostel Shanghai
voyage.address: 450 Middle Jiangxi Rd 上海市黄浦区江西中路450号
voyage.content: Another supurbly located hostel only moments from the Bund. Excellent beds, friendly staff (several with good English skills). Relaxed atmosphere, bar with free pool and DVDs. Three free internet terminals. Hot water is turned off noon-7PM. This hostel will also arrange train/aeroplane tickets. Airport pickup is possible.

voyage.name: Hongkong Hotel
voyage.content: If all the youth hostels are fully booked, which happens frequently, this is the next cheapest option on the Bund.

voyage.name: Jinjiang Inn "South Fujian"
voyage.price: from ¥200 (single room) to ¥320 (family room) per night.
voyage.content: Near the Old City, about a 15 minute walk from People's square. The hotel is entirely renovated, and offers very clean rooms with TV and Internet connection.

voyage.name: Shanghai YMCA
voyage.price: starting at US$15 for a dormitory and US$55 for a single room.
voyage.content: Comfortable rooms at a good quality price.

voyage.name: Green Court Serviced Apartment
voyage.content: This apart'hotel is located in People's Square, close to the Shanghai Municipal Government Building, Huaihai Road shopping district and Shanghai Museum. Each apartment, ranging from studios to two-bedroom apartments has a kitchen, living room, fitted bathroom, and Wi-Fi access.

voyage.name: Jin Jiang East Asia Hotel
voyage.content: Offers 164 refurbished rooms, all of which have air-conditioning, satellite TV, and high-speed Internet access. Some of its amenities include The Magnolia Hall that can accommodate up to 50 guests theater-style; business center that offers copy service, courier, fax, printing; and concierge that assists in airline, car rental, and tour inquiries.

voyage.name: Magnificent International Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel offers 182 rooms, of which 13 are suites, this hotel has of one of the best locations in the Huangpu District. It's a 15-min walk from the Huang Pi Road Subway Station, and is within proximity of business and conference venues, shopping districts, and cultural attractions such as The Bund and the Yuyuan Garden.

voyage.name: Metropole Hotel Jin Jiang
voyage.address: 180 Jiang Xi Rd (Middle) 上海市黄浦区江西中路180号
voyage.content: This splendid 1930 Art Deco hotel offers 137 rooms and has facilities such as a Chinese restaurant, a lobby bar, and number of conference and meeting facilities. Centrally located, just 0.5 km (0.3 mi) away from The Bund, and easily accessible from Shanghai International Convention Center.

voyage.name: Nanjing Hotel Shanghai Jin Jiang
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at ¥300
voyage.content: It offers 165 air-conditioned guestrooms, all of which have mini-bar, cable TV, and room safe. Their restaurant called Shanghai Town serves Beijing and Shanghai cuisines.

voyage.name: Pacific Hotel
voyage.content: Offers air-conditioned rooms, all of which have room safe, telephone with voice mail, and high-speed Internet access. Some of its amenities include Jinmen Club (spa and beauty salon), badminton and swimming facilities, and free shuttle bus to and from Hongqiao Airport.

voyage.name: Shanghai Hundred Centuries Hotel
voyage.content: Offers 94 air-conditioned rooms with mini bar, television, telephone, and free high speed Internet access.

voyage.name: Shanghai Yinbo Hotel
voyage.address: 135 Tiantong Rd 上海市虹口区天潼路135号
voyage.content: Typical nondescript mid range hotel located across the bridge on the north side of the Bund.

voyage.name: The Topsun on The Bund
voyage.content: Four-star hotel, situated north of the bustling business area where many of Shanghai’s largest financial establishments, businesses, and foreign consulates can be found.

voyage.name: Hyatt on the Bund
voyage.content: 5 star hotel opened in 2007 as part of the Grand Hyatt brand. Equipped with state of the art business and meeting facilities including 2 ballrooms and a glasshouse for special events.

voyage.name: Le Royal Méridien Shanghai
voyage.content: The hotel is located on Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, surrounded by popular shopping malls and other business outlets with only a short walk away to the Bund. This 66-storey building offers 761 guest rooms with views of the Huangpu River, People’s Square, or the Shanghai skyline. The hotel is in modern French style and offers diverse cuisine choices from its 6 dining venues.

voyage.name: Les Suites Orient, Bund Shanghai
voyage.content: Right on the Bund opposite the ferry terminal, the Les Suites Orient lives up to its name. The free breakfast is not to be missed.

voyage.name: New Harbour Service Apartments
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at ¥464
voyage.content: 4-star hotel located close to it are The Bund, Yu Garden, and Shanghai Great Theatre. 255 rooms, all of which have air-conditioning, satellite TV, and a mini-bar with refrigerator. Amenities include Chinese, Japanese and Western restaurants, health club, and internet room.

voyage.name: Pacific Hotel
voyage.content: A convenient jump-off point for exploring Shanghai since it is located at the west end of Nanjing East Rd, near the Bund and several Shanghai landmarks.

voyage.name: Park Hotel
voyage.content: Tel. 6327 5225. Another Art Deco masterpiece, the Park Hotel was once the tallest building in the Far East with 22 soaring stories, but in today's Shanghai it looks like a refugee from Gotham City among the surrounding glass and steel skyscrapers. Convenient location, but the rooms with good views facing Nanjing Xilu and the Park also have to deal with the road's traffic noise. Doubles around US$100.

voyage.name: Peace Hotel
voyage.content: Shanghai's grand old hotel, in 1930s Art Deco style and ideally located on the Bund. Perhaps somewhat overpriced given the lacklustre facilities and the spotty service. It has, however, a great cafe where you can enjoy a cup of coffee, as well as some jazz music played by the famous "Old Men's Jazz Band" made up of old musicians who played in the same hotel in the 1930s. In 2007, the hotel closed for a 3 year renovat

voyage.name: Radisson Shanghai New World
voyage.content: This hotel is connected to the New World department store and has easy access to most of Shanghai via the Metro.

voyage.name: Salvo Hotel Shanghai
voyage.content: The first all-steel high-rise in the area covering The Bund, Huangpu River and Nanjing Road. This 5-star hotel features Spanish-style furnishings and diverse cuisines in each of its three restaurants.

voyage.name: Yun’s Paradise Hotel
voyage.address: 789 E Fuxing R (Junction of S Henan Rd)
voyage.content: Offers air-conditioned guestrooms, all of which have Philips LCD TV with satellite channels, premium beds draped in Picasso cotton beddings, and free high-speed Internet access. Some of its amenities include Yun’s Paradise Health Center, Yun’s Paradise Porch (sells various Jiangnan products), and Harvest Festival Restaurant (serves Jiangnan and Ningbo cuisines. It also features a banquet hall and private room).

voyage.name: City God Temple
voyage.alt: 城隍廟 Chénghuángmiào, Old City God Temple
voyage.content: A well-known Taoist temple at the centre of the Old City, one of the biggest examples of traditional Chinese architecture in Shanghai. You can find local snacks and food as well as other traditional Chinese decorations in the surrounding commercial area.

voyage.name: Old City Wall
voyage.content: The small surviving part of the Shanghai city wall. A prominent feature is Dajing Tower. If you want to see a larger and better preserved wall, go to nearby Suzhou, or Nanjing.

voyage.name: Jiu Qu Qiao Bridge
voyage.content: A zig-zagging bridge near the City God Temple, the present construction dates from the early 20th century.

voyage.name: Dongjiadu Cathedral
voyage.content: Built by Spanish Jesuits in the 19th century, the historic seat of the Bishop of Shanghai. A relatively small church near the river, outside the old city wall. In 2018 the church is surrounded by a huge construction site and it's closed.

voyage.name: Yu Garden
voyage.alt: 豫园 Yù Yuán "Garden of Contentment"
voyage.content: A traditional Chinese Ming-style private garden that was built in 1559 but ransacked and restored several times since then. Entrance price is worth it for the many exquisite Chinese pavilions, seemingly never-ending paths, and sculpted gardens within. Near the garden, the famous zigzag bridge and its teahouse (see Drink) can be visited. The bazaar near the garden is always crowded with tourists.

voyage.name: Chenxiang Ge Temple
voyage.content: A historic Buddhist temple, with a statue on the upper floor carved from a rare wood.

voyage.name: Baiyun Guan Temple
voyage.content: A Taoist temple. Look for the statue of the guardian spirit for your Chinese zodiac.

voyage.name: Xiaotayuan Mosque
voyage.content: A historic mosque that combines Chinese and Islamic architectural styles. Shanghai's largest mosque, with a separate women's mosque next door.

voyage.name: Wenmiao Temple
voyage.content: The Temple to Confucius, with Shanghai's most famous vintage book market.

voyage.name: City God Temple
voyage.content: The area around the Old City God Temple and the Yuyuan Gardens has become a large commercial hub, with many restored historical buildings as well as new buildings in a somewhat traditional style. Take photos, shop for souvenirs, and enjoy the many restaurants and eateries. Enjoy an illuminated diorama or other forms of 19th century street side entertainment. Come after 6:30PM when the lights show off the beauty of th

voyage.name: Fuyou Antique Market
voyage.content: One of several multi-storey markets near Yuyuan metro station, at the northern end of the Old City - shop here for souvenirs, craft both modern and antique, as well as clothes and toys. Antiques are mainly in the lower basement floor of one of the buildings.

voyage.name: Shiliupu Fabric Market
voyage.content: A warren of tailor shops offering custom made clothes, from tuxedoes to dress shirts to fake designer jackets and qipao, the traditional Chinese dress with a slit up the thigh. The prices are cheap but expect a lot tinkering afterward as your tailor will not be able to remake something as you like unless you tell her exactly what you want. The tailoring itself is average. Bargain hard and be familiar with the prices

voyage.name: Nanxiang Steamed Bun Restaurant
voyage.content: Founded in 1900, this is the best-known restaurant specializing in small soup-filled buns called Xiaolongbao (also commonly referred to as "soup dumplings"), a characteristic Shanghai snack. This restaurant is popular for take-away and sit-down. The sit-down section (up the stairs) has a range of options - from the cheapest first floor dining room where you sit elbow-to-elbow with other patrons, to the "VIP section"

voyage.name: Ningbo Dumpling Shop
voyage.content: Another historic restaurant specializing in Ningbo-style Tangyuan ("rice dough balls" or, confusingly, also "soup dumplings"), another popular snack. This restaurant offers Tangyuan with fillings found almost nowhere else, both sweet and savoury. A separate counter offers a range of Shanghainese small dishes.

voyage.name: Mid-Lake Pavilion Teahouse
voyage.content: In the Yuyuan Gardens and reached by a 9-legged zigzag path to stop evil spirits. One of the most famous tea houses in all of China. A glass (not a pot) of your tea of choice is ¥20-25 downstairs and ¥40-55 upstairs — upstairs you'll get nice views, respite from the crowds, free snacks and even a souvenir or two. Pressure-free.

voyage.name: Jing'an Temple
voyage.content: This is a large Buddhist temple; the name translates as Temple of Peace and Tranquility. It is said to have been built in 247 CE, making it over 1750 years old.

voyage.name: Former residence of Chairman Mao Tse Tung
voyage.content: Small house in traditional style that housed Mao Tse Tung during his early days in the Chinese Communist Party. Preserved as a (very) small museum. Possibly the most interesting aspect is the fact that his once humble home is now surrounded by one of Shanghai's most expensive shopping malls full of luxury shops and hotels!

voyage.name: Jing'an Park
voyage.content: Nice public park with a lake and some walkways. A good place to see older Chinese people practice their dancing. If you play any Chinese board games — Chinese chess (xiangqi) or Go (weiqi) — there are often games going on in the Southeast corner of the park.

voyage.name: Shanghai Natural History Museum
voyage.price: ¥30 (standard adult ticket), ¥25 (visitors aged 60 to 69), ¥12 (children over 1.3 metres in height and full-time university students. Persons aged over 70 and children under 1.3 metres in height are granted free admission
voyage.hours: 08:50-17:15, closed on Mondays (except during Golden Weeks). Tickets are sold from 08:40 to 16:30

voyage.name: EVA Statue
voyage.content: The 25.06-meter-tall EVA Unit-01 statue holds the Guinness World Record as the largest anime sculpture in the world. Modelled after the iconic mecha from the Japanese anime Neon Genesis Evangelion, it is a free, permanent landmark.

voyage.name: Shanghai Acrobatics Show
voyage.content: All the impressive acts of a Chinese circus packed into one 90 minute show. The location is easy to walk by as the theater is hidden inside a hotel. Tickets are best bought in advance, especially for weekend shows. The good acts are up right from the start, so don't be late! An alternative is the Shanghai Circus in Zhabei.

voyage.name: Shanghai Exhibition Centre
voyage.alt: Sino-Soviet Friendship Building, 中苏友好大厦
voyage.content: Built in the 1950s and then the tallest building in Shanghai at 110 m, this is still a landmark.

voyage.name: Jingan Kerry Center
voyage.content: Very new shopping mall with lots of restaurants, clothes shops and an electronics store. Good cinema. In the basement is an Ole' supermarket (a top range China chain) which sells lots of good Western quality food at very high prices.

voyage.name: Reel Shanghai
voyage.content: Brand new upmarket mall with busy food court in the basement

voyage.name: Jiu Guang Shopping Mall
voyage.address: 1618 Nanjing Xi Lu, 南京西路1618号8楼, 近华山路
voyage.content: Launched in partnership with the Japanese Sogo chain, this mall has a distinctly Japanese feel to it. Food court in basement as well as 'Fresh Mart' supermarket.

voyage.name: Shanghai Centre
voyage.content: Three towers above an 8-story base. The base has quite a bit of high-end shopping, plus a supermarket in the basement with a range of imported foods. There is a pleasant coffee shop at ground level, back left corner as seen from the street. One tower has the Shanghai Ritz Carlton hotel; the others are apartments and offices, including several consulates. The complex also includes a theatre and an exhibition hall.

voyage.name: China Mobile
voyage.content: Get a mobile phone SIM or topup at this busy store on Nanjing Road

voyage.name: Saizeriya
voyage.content: One of a Japanese chain of Italian restaurants where a decently-sized plate of pasta can be had for less than ¥20 and all-you-can-drink soft drinks available for an additional ¥6 from 11AM-2PM. Menus are available in English.

voyage.name: CoCo Ichibanya
voyage.content: One of a Japanese chain of curry restaurants, with seafood, meat, and vegetarian curries available and variable levels of spiciness. There will be seasonal items on the menu that change depending on time of year. There is a spice rating from 1 (mild) to 5 (hot!); most people who like spicy food will be happy with 3, or perhaps 4. Others should chose 1 or 2 and consider ordering a larger serving of rice, which is also

voyage.name: Reel Food Court
voyage.content: Although not cheap by national standards, this is definitely a budget option in the Jing'an district. A clean and fairly large food court can be found next to Jing'An station in the basement of the Reel Shopping Mall, with fried dumplings to be had (4 for ¥6) to larger rice dishes and hotpots. Can be very busy.

voyage.name: Nanxiang Steamed Bun Restaurant
voyage.content: A branch of the famous xiaolongbao restaurant found in the Old City, but with significantly shorter lines.

voyage.name: Yang's Dumpling
voyage.content: Where the Nanxiang Steamed Bun Restaurant is known for its xiaolongbao, this place just around the corner is known for its shengjianbao, the fried version. Although there are several stores throughout Shanghai, this is the original, where it has been since 1994. Dumplings are made fresh to order, and there are other Shanghai specialties available. Can be busy during peak hours.

voyage.name: Bali Laguana
voyage.content: (巴厘岛), No.3 Jinan Park, 189 Huashan Road (near West Nanjing Road, 静安区华山路189号静安公园3号门 近南京西路). Standard Indonesian food served in a romantic and delightful setting overlooking a small pool that is particularly pretty at night.

voyage.name: Lavazza Coffee
voyage.content: Italian coffee shop with outdoor seating area. Good location for foreigners and Chinese to meet up for language exchanges. Free wifi and serves pasta.

voyage.name: Tonkatsu Qitiao
voyage.content: Japanese Ton Katsu restaurant which is somewhat more upmarket than CoCo Ichibanya.

voyage.name: Mr Harry Authentic British Restaurant
voyage.content: If you have been in China a while and want to enjoy a break with an English breakfast or fish and chips for lunch, then Mr Harry's is possibly the place for you. English pub style decorations and English beer available.

voyage.name: Dos Locos
voyage.address: Dos Locos - Suite B1-11, South Phase, 1515 Nanjing Xi Lu, near Changde Lu (静安嘉里中心, 南京西路1515号南区B1-11, 近常德路).
voyage.content: A copy of the Mexican-American chain, Chipotle, this restaurant serves large portions of burritos and tacos.

voyage.name: Beef and Liberty
voyage.address: Shanghai Centre, G/F, Shanghai Centre, No.1376 Nanjing Road
voyage.content: A 'premium' beefburger restaurant selling good tasting burgers at a high price.

voyage.name: Sumerian Coffee
voyage.address: 415 Shaanxi Bei Lu (near Beijing Xi Lu)
voyage.content: Offers coffee roasted on site (including coffee beans sourced from southern China) and nice wrap sandwiches.

voyage.name: Wagas
voyage.content: Related to the 'Baker and Spice' chain and serving fairly familiar Western food.

voyage.name: Wagas
voyage.content: Another branch of Wagas to the north of the temple

voyage.name: Pizza Express
voyage.content: The UK Pizza chain can be found in the Shanghai Centre. It is better tasting than the fast food pizza joints around Shanghai, albeit at a higher price.

voyage.name: Baker & Spice
voyage.address: Shanghai Centre, G/F, Shanghai Centre, No.1376 Nanjing Road
voyage.content: Another foreigner-friendly option in the Shanghai Centre. Free wifi. Opens at 07:30 which is convenient for early risers.

voyage.name: Just Grapes
voyage.content: Wine bar. It is also a wine store, and has an upstairs restaurant serving salads, pasta, and pizza. This is the perfect place to taste a glass of good wine at the bar or outside on the wooden patio

voyage.name: Dr Wine
voyage.content: Classic style of European wine bar, offering relaxed atmosphere and Italian anti-pasta

voyage.name: Uva Cafe
voyage.content: A wine bar aimed at the younger set.

voyage.name: Letour Traveler's Rest Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 上海乐途静安国际青年旅舍
voyage.content: A YHA bed and breakfast hostel in downtown Shanghai a 10-minute walk from Jing'an Temple. The building was built in 1930s as a towel factory and is deliberately refurbished to maintain its unique details: narrow lane (NongTang), Stone-frame, packing case etc. Price (normal season): Dorm bed ¥80, Private double ¥280, Private Twin or Triple a bit more. The hostel offers a lively vibrant atmosphere, including a

voyage.name: Shanghai Haigang Hotel
voyage.content: Near Pho Sizzling

voyage.name: Brightel All Suites Shanghai (Golden Tulip Ashar Suites Shanghai Central)
Howard Johnson All Suites Hotel Shanghai
voyage.alt: 上海绿地豪生全套房酒店; Shànghǎi lǜdìháo shēngquán tàofáng jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: No 1155, Yan'an W Rd (延安西路1155号; Yán'ān xīlù 1155 hào)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet. Also has a bar that can provide coffee and beer.

voyage.name: Jing'an Hotel Jin Jiang
voyage.content: A classic Spanish-style hotel. The hotel offers 126 aptly furnished rooms and a wealth of dining and leisure facilities. Business amenities include a fully equipped business center and meeting and conference venues.

voyage.name: JunAn Design Hotel
voyage.content: West side of Nanjing Rd. Opposite the hotel lies the famous Shanghai Television Tower. Rooms are air-conditioned, fitted with cable TV, hair dryer, and broadband Internet access. They also have a private bathroom and safe. Western and Chinese buffet breakfast is available.

voyage.name: Rendezvous Merry Hotel Shanghai
voyage.alt: 上海美丽园龙都大酒店; Shànghǎi měilì yuánlóng dōudà jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: No 396, Yan'an Rd W (延安西路396号; yán ān xī lù 396 hào)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet. The hotel has a Chinese and a Western restaurant and a bar that can provide coffee and beer. The hotel possesses various kinds of auxiliary facilities such as Chamber, Business Center, Currency exchange service, Shopping, Florist, Beauty Salon, Laundry, etc.

voyage.name: Shanghai Jin Chang Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. The Bund, Jade Buddha Temple, and Nanjing Rd are few of the places you can visit while staying at this hotel. They offer air-conditioned rooms that has a satellite TV, high-speed Internet, mini-bar, telephone, and smoke alarm.

voyage.name: Shanghai Yin Fa Hotel
voyage.content: Houses 72 air-conditioned rooms equipped with cable TV, telephone, electronic door locks, slippers, and electric kettle. Some of their facilities include conference rooms, health and fitness center, sauna, lobby bar, and game room. Li Yuan Restaurant serves Cantonese cuisine and can accommodate 130 guests.

voyage.name: Shanxi Business Hotel
voyage.content: It is located 15 km away from Hongqiao Airport. 178 air-conditioned rooms.

voyage.name: Shanghai Duxiana Hotel
voyage.address: No. 59 Wan Hang Du Hou Road
voyage.content: Rooms are equipped with Dux bed, 32-inch TV, Refrigerator and Air-conditioning. Some of its facilities and services are Business center, Meeting hall, Fitness room/gym and Free Wi-Fi Internet access.

voyage.name: Four Seasons
voyage.content: A favorite with business travelers, the Four Seasons is a luxury hotel with excellent amenities and several in-hotel dining options. The breakfast buffet is lavish, though typical of high-end Shanghai hotels. Given the cost (¥225) consider upgrading to the Executive Club Lounge (not to be confused with the "Executive Suite") where you get free cooked breakfast on the 37th floor.

voyage.name: Ivy Shanghai
voyage.content: The 5-star hotel offers very intimate service for each of its 45 rooms and suites. Each floor is assigned a butler, business amenities abound, and the hotel boasts a Teppanyaki restaurant.

voyage.name: Park Hotel
voyage.content: An Art Deco masterpiece, it was once the tallest building in the Far East with 22 soaring stories, but in today's Shanghai it looks like a refugee from Gotham City among the surrounding glass and steel skyscrapers. Convenient location, but the rooms with good views facing Nanjing Xilu and the Park also have to deal with the road's traffic noise.

voyage.name: Shanghai Hotel Jin Jiang
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Skiline - World Union Service Apartment
voyage.content: Studio, Twin Bed and Suite, all equipped with Air-conditioning, Cable TV and High-speed Internet access. Facilities and services are Business centre, Airport transfer and Travel agency.

voyage.name: World Union Service Apartment
voyage.address: Room 1601, 16 F, No 199. Wu Lu Mu Qi Road (North)
voyage.content: It offers standard and superior suite, all equipped with air-conditioning, TV with cable channels, and living room. Some of its facilities and services are business center, meeting room, and high-speed Internet access.

voyage.name: Ladoll Service Apartment
voyage.address: Room 201, 2nd Floor, No 268. Yu Yuan Road
voyage.content: It offers standard, superior, and deluxe suite, all equipped with cable TV, DVD, telephone, and high-speed Internet connection. Some of its facilities and services are meeting room, business centre, and airport and city transfers.

voyage.name: Fuxing Road
voyage.content: Walk along Fuxing Rd to see classical old buildings and much boutique shopping. The Shanghai Music Conservatory is near Fuxing Road. Some blocks west of Shaanxi Road here and there are a number of shops specialising in musical instruments, especially orchestral stringed instruments, and several shops for classical or jazz recordings.

voyage.name: Fuxing Park
voyage.address: 105 Fuxing Zhong Rd (卢湾区复兴中路105号; Lúwānqū Fùxīngzhōnglù)
voyage.content: This European-style park formerly known as French Park has gardens, open spaces and restaurants and clubs dotted throughout. Early in the morning, the park is filled with dancers (some Chinese styles, but mainly Western ballroom) players of various games (cards, mahjong, Chinese chess and Go), Tai Chi artists, and singing groups.

voyage.name: Former Site of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea
voyage.alt: 大韩民国临时政府旧址/대한민국 임시정부 상해 유적지
voyage.address: No. 4 Lane 306, Madang Road, Huangpu District (黄浦区马当路306弄4号)
voyage.content: In 1919, during the Japanese occupation of Korea, Korean independence activists in Shanghai established the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea. This building served as the provisional government's main headquarters from 1926 to 1932. The site is now owned and preserved as a museum by South Korea. Everything is explained in Chinese and Korean, and there's nothing in English.

voyage.name: Shanghai Museum of Arts and Crafts
voyage.content: Inside of this renaissance building you can see ivory, jade and wood carvings, art on textiles, paper cutting, and folk crafts as well as artisans at work.

voyage.name: Museum for Oriental Musical Instruments
voyage.address: Ground Floor, Art Education Building, Shanghai Conservatory of Music, 1189 Huaihai Middle Road, Xuhui District (徐汇区淮海中路1189号, 上海音乐学院美育楼一楼)
voyage.content: A museum run by the Shanghai Conservatory of Music. It has a collection of around 800 musical instruments from over 40 countries. Visitors are required to make a booking on the museum’s WeChat account before visiting the museum.

voyage.name: Shanghai Propaganda Poster Art Centre (PPAC)
voyage.alt: 上海杨培明宣传画收藏艺术馆
voyage.address: Building 7 Block K, 726 Yan'an Rd (W) 上海市长宁区延安西路726号7楼K座
voyage.content: This private collection is one of the most relevant and uncensored exhibits available to visitors interested in a glimpse of the politics and art of Mao-era China. Posters, memorabilia, photos, and even "大字报" (dazibao: big character posters) can be found in rotating exhibition. Due to the controversial nature of the historical items stored here, the museum is quite difficult to find, and unlabeled from the outside. W

voyage.name: Yongping Lane
voyage.content: One of the secret gems on Hengshan Road is a lane open to the public. It includes 'Colca Peru Spanish Restaurant', other Western food and drinks, a temporary art & fashion market along the zig-zagged lane, and the 'Yongjia Road 690 exhibition hall'. The lane goes from behind exit 4 of Hengshan Road station (line ), and exits at no. 690, Yongjia Road.

voyage.name: K11 Sky Garden
voyage.content: If you are on a low budget or you want to have some free fun, buy some cheap drinks in a grocery and go up by elevator to the 6th floor of the 61-floor K11 skyscraper. Then you turn right and right again, to find one of the two sky gardens (the other one is left and left), with empty tables and chairs and a nice view on the city. Best timing for this secret place is at evening with your partner and ideally full moon.

voyage.name: Wukang Mansion
voyage.content: A protected historic apartment building in French Renaissance style completed in 1924 that has been the residence of many celebrities.

voyage.name: Site of the First National Congress of the CPC
voyage.content: The building where the Communist Party of China (CPC) had their first national meeting in 1921.

voyage.name: Zhou Enlai's Former Residence
voyage.content: This was the Shanghai Office of the Communist Party from June 1946. It is now a museum telling the story of the Communist revolution in China and particularly Shanghai. See #Sinan Mansions above.

voyage.name: Sun Yat-sen's Former Residence
voyage.content: Sun Yat-sen (Sun Zhong Shan in Mandarin) was the first leader of the Republic of China after the 1911 revolution that overthrew the Qing Dynasty. He is one of the very few political figures regarded favorably by the current governments of both China and Taiwan. He lived mainly in Nanjing, the capital at the time, but also had this house in Shanghai. It was converted into a museum in 1961.

voyage.name: Soong Ching-ling's Former Residence
voyage.price: ¥20 (adults), ¥10 (students and persons aged between 60 and 70), Children, disabled people and persons aged over 70 may enter for free
voyage.content: Soong Ching-ling was Sun Yat-sen's wife and a significant political figure in her own right.Like her father, brothers and sisters, she went to an American university (Wesleyan College in Macon, Georgia), spoke excellent English, and was deeply involved in Kuomintang politics prior to the Kuomintang defeat in 1949. She negotiated Chiang Kai Shek's release when he was locked up during the Xi'an Incident. Unlike her sib

voyage.name: Xujiahui junction
voyage.content: A large road junction with Xujiahui metro station (lines , and ) underneath it.

voyage.name: Shanghai Jiaotong University
voyage.content: This is one of China's top technical schools. The new main campus is in Minhang, but the original campus in the French Concession is still used; it now does mainly continuing education courses such as Chinese-for-foreigners or MBA-for-executives

voyage.name: Guangqi Park and Memorial Hall
voyage.content: The park was built around the tomb of Xu Guangqi, a prominent scholar and China's most notable Catholic convert, after whom the Xujiahui area and the Xuhui district are ultimately named. The tomb, restored according to its original set-up, is a curious combination of a large Christian cross as the grave marker, with a traditional Chinese "spirit way" lined with stone animals. The park features a lake, a bridge, a car

voyage.name: St. Ignatius Cathedral
voyage.content: The area was under renovation in 2018, but the cathedral is open. Don't wear slippers or anything that resembles it, they are strict on decent outfit rules.

voyage.name: Xujiahui Park
voyage.content: On the location of a former brick factory now stands the Xujiahui Park, which contains a man-made meandering brook (modelling in miniature the course of the Huangpu River), a lake with two black swans, basketball courts, and a children's playground.

voyage.name: Former site of Pathé
voyage.content: The Red House, which once housed the Pathé China record company, is at the edge of Xujiahui Park.

voyage.name: Metro station exhibition
voyage.content: Small, free museum exhibition at Shanghai Xujiahui station between exits 5 and 7. The exhibits are changed several times a year and sometimes English explanations are included. The history or tradition-related items are brought from nearby museums.

voyage.name: Shanghai Film Museum
voyage.content: Starting from 1896, Shanghai has had a prominent role in Chinese movie making. German architect Tilman Thürmer transformed a film studio into an exciting experience of film evolution through over 70 interactive installations and thousands of historic exhibits. The museum contains 4 main exhibition units (floors) and an art cinema. (A very small free permanent exhibition can be seen in Shanghai Indoor Stadium metro st

voyage.name: Longhua Temple
voyage.content: One of the city's less-visited temples for foreign visitors, but an important one and one of the most popular for Shanghai residents during religious festivals. It is one of the largest ancient Buddhist temples in Shanghai. The first temple was built in 247 CE, but it was destroyed and rebuilt under the Song dynasty, 977 CE, and several times since then. It is a temple of the Ch'an sect of Buddhism, better known in t

voyage.name: Longhua Martyrs' Cemetery
voyage.content: Longhua Temple's old garden and orchard has now been converted into this large green space. Very few people are buried here, so it's more of a memorial garden and museum but the acreage is beautiful and large, akin to Luxun Park. The temple grounds became a "cemetery" because, during the civil war, Koumintang troops executed Communists on these grounds and the cemetery, poetry, fountains, steles, and sculptures comme

voyage.name: Long Museum West Bund
voyage.alt: Dragon Art Museum West Bund Branch, 龙美术馆西岸馆
voyage.content: The West Bund branch of the private art museum established by the wealthy collectors Liu Yiqian and his wife Wang Wei. The museum also has branches in Pudong District and the western city of Chongqing. Groups of 26 people or more are required to make a reservation at least 2 days before their visit.

voyage.name: West Bund Art Center
voyage.address: 2555 Longteng Avenue, Xuhui District (徐汇区龙腾大道2555号)
voyage.content: Fees and opening times vary. See individual listings below.

voyage.name: Centre Pompidou and West Bund Museum
voyage.alt: 西岸美术馆与蓬皮杜中心
voyage.price: On weekdays, tickets are ¥70 for the semi-permanent exhibitions, ¥90 for the temporary exhibitions and ¥150 for all exhibitions. On weekends and public holidays, the tickets prices are increased to ¥80 for the semi-permanent exhibitions, ¥100 for the temporary exhibitions and ¥170 for all exhibitions
voyage.hours: First floor and basement open 10:00-22:00. Second floor open 10:00-17:00 (last entry at 16:00) but closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 2600 Longteng Avenue, Xuhui District (徐汇区龙腾大道2600号)

voyage.name: Shanghai Center of Photography
voyage.hours: 10:30-17:30, no entry after 17:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 1/2555 Longteng Avenue, Xuhui District (徐汇区龙腾大道2555号-1)

voyage.name: Yuz Museum
voyage.price: Tickets for the art and film studios are ¥100. Entry to the 'Open Feast' area is free
voyage.hours: 10:00-21:00, no entry after 20:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 35 Fenggu Road, Xuhui District (徐汇区丰谷路35号)

voyage.name: Tank Shanghai
voyage.price: Ticket prices vary according to the exhibitions being held. A one-year membership card costs ¥360.
voyage.hours: 10:00-18:00, no entry after 17:30, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 2380 Longteng Avenue, Xuhui District (徐汇区龙腾大道2380号)
voyage.content: Another art museum.

voyage.name: Shanghai Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Covering 81.86 hectares, the garden has a diverse collection of Chinese plants. Its sections are the penjing (bonsai) garden, penjing museum, tropicarium, magnolia, peony, bamboo and conifer gardens.

voyage.name: Guilin Park
voyage.content: A relatively small park with traditional Chinese gates, curved paths and pavilions. Good park for a walk if you happen to be nearby, but for genuine historical gardens you can consider travelling to Suzhou.

voyage.name: Kangjian Park
voyage.content: larger and more modern than Guilin Park

voyage.name: Shanghai Normal University
voyage.content: The Shanghai Normal University Xuhui Campus lies on both sides of Guilin Road, not far from Guilin Park. The east side features a lake and the west side is also pleasant for a walk.

voyage.name: Chinese "Comfort Women" History Museum
voyage.alt: 中国“慰安妇”历史博物馆
voyage.address: Level 2, Wenyuan Building, Shanghai Normal University Xuhui Campus East Side (上海师范大学徐汇校区东部文苑楼2楼)
voyage.content: A museum about the women who were forced into sexual slavery by the Japanese army during the Second World War.

voyage.name: Jinjiang Amusement Park
voyage.content: Has a 108-metre (354 ft) Ferris wheel with, on a clear day, a fine view over the city.

voyage.name: Diva Life Nail & Beauty Lounge
voyage.content: A house, mixed with Chinese and European style. Established in 1933, this three story complex was once the home of the Jewish wine merchant H.L. Menken.

voyage.name: Ferguson Lane
voyage.content: A 1930s building filled with restaurants and boutique shops.

voyage.name: Garden Books
voyage.content: Good selection of Chinese travel guides, aromatic coffee, and flavorful ice cream. Their monthly bric-a-brac sales are a popular local social event.

voyage.name: Madame Mao's Dowry
voyage.content: Cultural Revolution nostalgia. Prices are stiff enough that buying here is recommended only if cheaper places do not have what you want.

voyage.name: Silk qipao shops
voyage.content: A row of shops along Chang Le Lu, between Mao Ming Lu and Shan Xi Nan Lu specializes in silk Qi Paos (traditional Shanghai-style silk dresses), which can be made to measure. The shops are especially popular with Japanese visitors staying at the nearby Okura Garden Hotel. An alternative destination for qipao in Shanghai is along North Shaanxi Road, near the junction with West Nanjing Road, where the most famous qipao

voyage.name: Spin Ceramics
voyage.content: Designer ceramics by Chinese artists but with a Japanese flavor, in a stylish minimalist space.

voyage.name: Torana House
voyage.content: Has Tibetan and Chinese carpets and Tibetan furniture in a contemporary gallery.

voyage.name: Pottery Workshop Shanghai
voyage.content: Second location for this shop.

voyage.name: IAPM Mall
voyage.content: This upscale mall houses big-name boutiques, restaurants and cafes. It features an atrium famous for its large-scale decoration exhibits during (Chinese and western) holidays.

voyage.name: Dongtai Road Antique Market
voyage.content: The largest antique market in the city, and the cheapest provided you bargain hard.

voyage.name: Vegetarian Lifestyle
voyage.content: A beautifully appointed modern restaurant where everything is vegetarian. You will not find much in the way of fake meat that pervades most of the other vegetarian places. Instead, you will enjoy beautifully cooked dishes from all over the country in addition to a juice bar.

voyage.name: Spicy Joint
voyage.address: 3/F, K. Wah Center, 1028 Middle Huaihai Rd, near Donghu Rd (淮海中路1028号, 嘉华中心嘉华坊3楼, 近东湖路)
voyage.content: Ridiculously popular for their cheap stylized Sichuan food, in a young and fashionable environment. The waits for a table are notorious.

voyage.name: Foodrepublic Food Court
voyage.content: Food court with many different restaurants. Most do not accept cash, though the restaurants that have their own separate seating area take both cash and cards, so you will have to add money to and put down a deposit for a stored-value card specific to the other Foodrepublics. You can see plastic models of all the dishes before you order them, so you will have a decent idea of what you are getting. Copious MSG (avoida

voyage.name: Ah Da's Spring Onion Pancakes
voyage.content: This humble stall moved here from another part of the French Concession. It sells hot cong you bing, and is a Shanghai establishment. Owner Wu Gencheng has been selling his creations for over 30 years. Queues can be notoriously long (up to 3 hours), and they frequently run out before closing time, so come early.

voyage.name: Amokka
voyage.content: Coffee bar and restaurant good for lunch stops.

voyage.name: Cafe Dan
voyage.address: No. 41, Lane 248 Taikang Lu, near Sinan Lu 泰康路248弄41号, 近思南路
voyage.content: Japanese style coffee house with very good tasting coffee and very nice Hokkaido Cheese Cake.

voyage.name: Cantina Agave
voyage.address: 291 Fumin Road, corner of Changle Road
voyage.content: Good Mexican food, beer and cocktails. They have another location in Pudong.

voyage.name: Di Shui Dong
voyage.content: Fiery cuisine from Hunan, the birthplace of Mao Zedong, thus a menu full of "Mao's Shrimp", "Mao's Chicken" and such. Very popular with foreigners.

voyage.name: Enoterra
voyage.content: Excellent wine bar specializing in Argentinean and South African wines. Food is fairly basic with cheese and meat plates and salads, but the wine is outstanding.

voyage.name: Hailaogui
voyage.content: Cafe specialising in sweet Chinese desserts claimed to have all sorts of beneficial effects for your health, particularly dishes made with turtle. No English menu.

voyage.name: Secret Garden
voyage.content: Serving Cantonese food in pleasant surroundings. The veranda-like space near to Secret Garden has been home to a succession of restaurants, the latest incarnation being a Greek restaurant.

voyage.name: Shanghai Uncle
voyage.content: A famous chain of three restaurants known for Shanghai flair with some Western accents. Known for their spare ribs, smoked fish and fatty pork with garlic.

voyage.name: Uighur Restaurant
voyage.content: Claims to be the "original" Xinjiang cuisine restaurant in the city, and probably the best-known. The typical main dishes are moderately spicy preparations of lamb, but the menu also features some rather adventurous items like camel feet, sheep's eyeballs, and a bull's you-know-what. Also music and dance shows with the obligatory audience participation.

voyage.name: Glo London
voyage.content: An English style restaurant that does familiar (for westerners) style brunch. Rather expensive, but the food tastes pretty close to what you would get in a good restaurant in England. Coffee shop and a good bakery on the ground floor (half price on many items after 21:00), a disco-ish bar on the next floor, then a grill restaurant, and finally a rooftop barbeque. Nearby metro stops: go north along Wulumuqi for Line 1

voyage.name: ASE Mall
voyage.content: A huge mall finished in 2017, hosting mostly elite and highly decorated restaurants, Will's Fitness and a cinema. The building features a panoramic elevator, an inner yard, and neon signs that resemble old shopping streets.

voyage.name: Casanova
voyage.address: far western end of Julu Rd
voyage.content: Very competent Italian fare.

voyage.name: Le Saleya
voyage.price: Prix fixe menu is ¥220 per person
voyage.content: Neighborhood French Restaurant. Unpretentious and you can close your eyes and imagine you are on the Ile de la Cite.

voyage.name: Mesa
voyage.content: Excellent and flavorful Western and fusion food accented by a fine wine list. The stunning view from the balcony is at its best in the spring and fall.

voyage.name: Otto
voyage.content: A sophisticated Italian restaurant and wine bar.

voyage.name: Sasha's
voyage.content: European-style food in a lovely old mansion. Large patio area.

voyage.name: Shintori
voyage.content: Japanese design restaurant with stunning features. Serving traditional and fusion cuisine.

voyage.name: Southern Belle
voyage.content: Good American food including some Tex-Mex dishes. The biscuits are disappointing, the mint juleps just fine.

voyage.name: Wooden Paradise
voyage.address: No. 3, Lane 63 Fuxing Xi Lu, near Yongfu Lu
voyage.content: Great little cocktail bar; the entrance is at the back of the bar.

voyage.name: Boxing Cat Brewery
voyage.address: 82 Fuxing Xi Lu, near Yongfu Lu
voyage.content: This popular bar & restaurant provides pub grub & a decent selection of beers, including house beers. It also has an outdoor area that's popular.

voyage.name: Senator Saloon
voyage.address: 98 Wuyuan Lu, near Wulumuqi Zhong Lu
voyage.content: A craft cocktail bar from the same people as Sichuan Citizen. Lots of choices with a particular focus on bourbon.

voyage.name: Jenny's Blue Bar
voyage.content: A friendly bar, run by Jenny in its present location since 2000. A wide choice of drinks, good music and sports coverage mean that it is popular both with expats and with visitors. Look out for the two cats that make themselves at home behind the bar, frequently sleeping on top of the television or the display units.

voyage.name: Oscar's Pub
voyage.content: Mainly an expat bar, in an area with several others. Dartboard, chess on Sundays, reasonable food and a range of drinks, a Filipino band. Cheap Tiger in happy hour, 11:00-20:00.

voyage.name: Shanghai Brewery
voyage.content: A brew pub with western food, big-screen TVs and English-speaking staff.

voyage.name: Le Café des Stagiaires (Found 158)
voyage.content: Popular French bar & restaurant in the sprawling Found 158 complex. Complete with French comfort food.

voyage.name: Daga Brewpub
voyage.content: Busy brewpub with a wide selection of beers. The pub places an emphasis on good quality Chinese beers but also has an impressive selection from the US & elsewhere. Serves food too.

voyage.name: The Refinery
voyage.address: 181 Taicang Lu, near Huangpi Nan Lu
voyage.content: This craft beer bar & restaurant in the upmarket Xintiandi bar and dining complex is a popular choice for expats and tourists. It's just south of the fountain in Xintiandi.

voyage.name: Asset Hotel Shanghai
voyage.content: The hotel is close to well-known places such as Xujiahui and Zhaojiabang Rd. All rooms are air-conditioned and have their own private bathroom. Services include 24-hour front desk and room services, and free shuttle bus is offered to guests who want to explore the rest of the district.

voyage.name: Blue Mountain Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 上海蓝山国际青年旅舍
voyage.address: 2F Bldg #1, 1072 Nong, Quxi Rd, Luwan District (卢湾区瞿溪路1072弄1号甲二楼)
voyage.content: On the street just outside you will find several restaurants, small supermarkets, and fruitshops. The staff is helpful and speaks good English.

voyage.name: Shanghai Bin Guan
voyage.content: If you took a bus to Shanghai South Station, this is a decent hotel within walking distance, you have to go through the underpass. have massage in your room if you want. It is very far South of the French Concession: two subway stops or taxi from Xujiahui.

voyage.name: Anting Villa Hotel
voyage.content: Offers guestrooms equipped with air-conditioning, cable television (with lots of English channels), and an IDD phone. It is a must-try to dine in at their very own Maple Leaves Restaurant, that serves Shanghainese and Cantonese cuisines all day. It is in a beautiful, sleepy Concession neighborhood, down the road from the popular bar Cotton's, and close to subway lines 1, 7 and 9. The hotel is used for many special oc

voyage.name: Hua Ting Hotel
voyage.content: A 5-star hotel, is also not far away, you may take Metro Line 1 for one stop and get off at Shanghai Stadium, the hotel is close to the metro station. It is not in the French Concession, but one stop or by taxi away.

voyage.name: Jianguo Hotel
voyage.content: Offers 454 air-conditioned guestrooms, all of which have high-speed Internet, TV, mini-bar, and room safe. Some of its amenities include fitness center/gym, sauna, and an indoor pool. Restaurants include the CTC Restaurant that is known for its shark's fin, abalone, and other upscale Chinese delicacies; Shanghai Restaurant that serves authentic Shanghai dishes during lunch and dinner; and Yuliu Restaurant that serves

voyage.name: Jin Jiang Tian Cheng Hotel
voyage.address: 585 Xujiahui Rd, The East Building, Jin Yu Lan Sq
voyage.content: Four-star business hotel with 148 guestrooms. Business and event facilities include a business center and event and conference venues of varying sizes. Leisure offerings include indoor swimming pool, disco and karaoke center. It is just south of the French Concession.

voyage.name: Patina Court
voyage.content: All rooms equipped with air-conditioning, cable TV and internet connection. Some of its facilities and services are Swimming pool, sauna, massage service, room service, bar, cafe, Meeting facilities and business center.

voyage.name: San Want Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star hotel with 383 rooms with LCD TV, Japanese-style bathtub, refrigerator, and high-speed Internet access. Conference rooms, banquet hall and business center available. It is to the far southwest of the French Concession.

voyage.name: Somerset Xu Hui Shanghai
voyage.alt: 上海徐汇盛捷服务公寓
voyage.address: No 888 Shaanxi Nan Road, Xu Hui district
voyage.content: Each of the 167 residences at Somerset Xu Hui is furnished with fully-equipped kitchens, home entertainment system and broadband Internet access.

voyage.name: Sports Hotel
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at
voyage.content: Four-stars. Outside the hotel are nearby tourist spots such as Shanghai Museum, People’s Square, and Yu Garden. Their guestrooms are equipped with air conditioning, a 25-inch cable TV, and electronic door locks. Some of their offered facilities includes an indoor swimming pool, gymnasium, sauna, and function and business rooms. It is halfway between Shanghai Stadium and Xujiahui Metro Station.

voyage.name: Andaz Shanghai
voyage.content: Andaz are Hyatt's boutique hotels; this is the first one in Asia.

voyage.name: Ascott Huai Hai Road Shanghai
voyage.alt: 上海雅诗阁淮海路服务公寓
voyage.address: No 282, Huaihai Road Central, Luwan district
voyage.content: The serviced residence is in the Luwan District near Xintiandi. It studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom apartments, each with its own kitchen, washing machine, home entertainment system and modern furnishings.

voyage.name: Garden Avenue Hotel
voyage.content: 5-star business hotel nowhere near Shanghai’s central business district. It has 218 rooms, fully-equipped banquet halls, and dining and recreational facilities. It is next to the South Railway Station and taxi away from Xujiahui.

voyage.name: Hengshan Moller Villa
voyage.content: Housed in a stunning piece of 1936 architecture. Rooms are frequently booked out so be sure to try to get one of the main rooms which contain wood panelling or business rooms that are much larger and come with a huge balcony that overlooks the garden.

voyage.name: Hengshan Picardie Hotel
voyage.content: A classic Art Deco-inspired hotel in the heart of French Concession. The hotel offers 254 rooms and dining and leisure facilities. Business amenities include a fully-equipped business center and venues such as Kaixuan Palace and Blossom Hall.

voyage.name: The Kunlun Jing An
voyage.content: While still popular with business travelers for its recognizable name, the Hilton Shanghai has lost some of its luster, although it's still considered a top end hotel in this area. Rooms are spacious and modern, and the staff are friendly, but the Hilton needs to step up its game.

voyage.name: Jin Jiang Hotel
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at
voyage.content: Offers 434 luxurious rooms, all of which have individually controlled air-conditioning, mini-bar, TV with cable channels, DVD player, and refrigerator. Some of its amenities include fitness center, beauty salon, spa, sauna, and massage service.

voyage.name: Jin Jiang Tower
voyage.content: Five-star hotel on Changle Road.

voyage.name: Lanson Place Jinlin Tiandi Residences Shanghai
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at
voyage.address: No 3, Lane 168 Xingye Rd, Luwan District
voyage.content: Offers 3-bedroom residences with engaging views, either over the alleyways of the Xintiandi quarter or a tranquil lake. All apartments are equipped with air-conditioning, cable TV, fully equipped kitchen, and Internet connection. Some of its amenities include a home theater system, sauna and steam rooms, and a fully equipped gymnasium.

voyage.name: Mason Hotel
voyage.address: 935 Central Huaihai Rd, Luwan, French Concession
voyage.content: This boutique hotel is cozy and comfortable and great for quiet nights sleep. All rooms have internet access and there's a 2nd-floor lounge, a rooftop beer garden, a variety of restaurants and a Starbucks on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Okura Garden Hotel
voyage.content: 5-star hotel built around the former French Club and its garden from 1926. Many art-deco decorations from that time are still visible in the hotel, especially in the Ball Room. Very central location along Huai Hai Road, with good accessibility and a subway stop (South Shaanxi Road, Line 1) next to the hotel grounds.

voyage.name: Old House Inn
voyage.content: With only a dozen rooms, it's advisable to book ahead to secure one of these charming rooms, furnished in traditional Chinese style. All rooms have internet access and breakfast, which is included, is served in an outdoor courtyard.

voyage.name: Royal Court Hotel Shanghai
voyage.address: Lane 622, 7 Middle Huaihai Rd, Luwan District
voyage.content: A five star business hotel. Air-conditioned rooms, conference halls, restaurant and bar, gym and sauna. Easily accessible from S Shanxi Rd Stn and Nanjing Rd.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Shanghai Ruijin
voyage.content: Villa-style hotel with picturesque surroundings. All of the 5 villas are designed in French style, some harking back to the start of the 20th century. The main building is particularly nice with a grand colonial vista. The hotel sits in a park-like compound with small bridges, ponds, pavilions and marble fountains.

voyage.name: Shanghai New-Westlake Hotel
voyage.address: No 22, Lane 133, Mao Ming South Road, Luwan District
voyage.content: It is 5 km from the railway station. It offers 20 air-conditioned rooms with cable TV, free broadband Internet access, a private toilet, and a room safe.

voyage.name: Pullman Shanghai Skyway
voyage.content: The hotel impresses the most with its sheer size - over 50 floors, crowned by a gargantuan canopy, make it a visible landmark from much of southern Shanghai. The smallest rooms in the hotel are almost 50 m² in size. On the inside, it is getting quite long in the tooth and gradual renovations slowly bring it in line with more modern Pullmans, but all of the features you'd expect of one are here, including a swimming p

voyage.name: Langham Xintiandi
voyage.content: Luxury hotel right next to the Xintiandi old town.

voyage.name: Fudan University
voyage.content: There are two campuses in Yangpu District, the older, main campus, just west of Wujiaochang, and the newer Jiangwan campus, in New Jiangwan Town (新江湾城). The main campus of Fudan University is a 10- to 15-minute walk west of Wujiaochang along Handan Road (邯郸路). Alternatively, you can take one of the numerous buses west along Handan Road (such as buses 59, 749, or 942) to the front gates of Fudan University. In the mai

voyage.name: Tongji University
voyage.content: The main campus is in Yangpu District. The university is served by the Tongji University station (同济大学站) of Metro Line 10, which brings you to the southeast gate of the university, facing Siping Road (四平路).

voyage.name: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
voyage.content: North of Fudan University's main campus. You can reach it by taking buses 406 or 819 from Wujiaochang.

voyage.name: Shanghai Institute of Physical Education
voyage.content: The main attractions of note at this university are the Chinese Martial Arts Museum (中国武术博物馆) and the old government building of the city of Shanghai (旧上海特别市政府), constructed in 1933, now an administration building for the university. Yangpu was the site of the new government of Shanghai under the Republic of China's rule, and many government buildings were constructed in this area. To reach the campus, take bus 90 fr

voyage.name: National Anthem Gallery
voyage.alt: 国歌展示馆 guógē zhǎnshì guǎn
voyage.content: Relics, artifacts and modern technology are used to tell in Chinese and English how the theme of a patriotic movie became the Chinese Anthem. You can include the gallery into a whole walk by the North Band and Shikumen Houses.

voyage.name: Gongqing Forest Park
voyage.price: ¥15, children under 1.2 metres free when accompanied by an adult. Activities inside the park cost extra. Separate bamboo garden (万竹园; literally Thousand bamboo garden) on the south side of Nenjiang Road is admission ¥20
voyage.address: Northeast corner of Nenjiang Road (嫩江路) and Jungong Road (军工路). Ticketing booth along Nenjiang Road just east of Jungong Road, or along Jungong Road north of Nenjiang Road.
voyage.content: A large forest park that provides an escape from the urban confines of the city. Great for picnics and relaxation. Features thrill coasters, miniature train ride, pleasure boats, mini-golf, bumper cars.

voyage.name: Wanda Plaza
voyage.content: It is the favorite entertainment spot for university students and locals on the north side. A good selection of restaurants can be found in the plaza, along with box stores and a cinema. This is the largest of Twanda Group's 14 malls in Shanghai.

voyage.name: Wal-Mart
voyage.content: Good place to stock up on supplies if you are in the area.

voyage.name: Ciao Cafe
voyage.content: Good (Asian style) pizza, pasta, good sandwiches and coffee. Nice atmosphere and popular with foreign students. Has delivery service.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Fudan
voyage.content: This is the most convenient full-service hotel to Fudan University. English-speaking staff aims to make your stay hassle-free. Suites are well-appointed, mattresses comfortable, rather than rock-hard. Lavish East/West buffet breakfast includes both hand-pulled noodles and Western pastries. Buffet dinner a less grand affair, but Western and Chinese à la carte menus are available. Excellent athletic facilities include

voyage.name: 1933 Shanghai
voyage.content: An abattoir with impressive architecture, built in colonial times, has been renovated into an artist centre, with a theatre, shops, cafes, restaurants and creative design buildings.

voyage.name: Shanghai Jewish Refugees Museum
voyage.content: The museum is at the site of what used to be the Ohel Moishe Synagogue. The synagogue was built in 1928 by Russian Jews and was one of the principal places of worship for Jewish refugees in Shanghai during the Second World War.

voyage.name: Shanghai Postal Museum
voyage.hours: Wed Thu Sat Sun 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00; closed Mon Tue Fri; on Wed Thu only the 2nd floor is open
voyage.content: Occupies the historic General Post Office Building, a landmark building that was built in 1924.

voyage.name: Lu Xun Park
voyage.content: This park provides a quiet spot for reading, meditation, and exercising, yet on the eastern side are plenty of rides small kids would enjoy and a lake with boats for rent. Lu Xun — one of the most important Chinese writers of the 20th century — is buried here and has both a memorial statue and clock in his honor. Mao was an admirer and did an inscription for the tomb. There is a tea shop near the north en

voyage.name: North Bund and Shikumen Houses
voyage.content: A pleasant walk would start from International Cruise Terminal metro station, line . Visit the Baiyulan Square Shopping Center to admire its architecture. Then head towards the river and a bit to the right, where you can climb and jump in the adventure park, both adults and children. Walk along the river bank towards east, you will find old pictures and stories about the wharf and see ships being loaded, as well as a

voyage.name: Red Square
voyage.content: Russian restaurant with authentic Russian dishes. Good atmosphere, OK food and slow service.

voyage.name: Sleeping Dragon Hostel
voyage.alt: 上海歇龙国际青年旅社
voyage.address: 394 Zhoushan Rd (舟山路394，虹口区，上海)
voyage.content: Youth hostel rooms and showers are very clean. There is a street market just outside of the hostel. The hostel is in a traditional Chinese area of Shanghai with a Jewish history from the early 20th century. Services, available in English, include travel planning, plane and train ticket booking. No curfew, laundry, reasonably priced drinks, books and DVDs for borrow, international calls from the front desk, free inter

voyage.name: Jiu Long Hotel Jin Jiang
voyage.content: The location is great to explore Shanghai’s cultural treasures and other places of interest. Shopaholics will be thrilled to know that this hotel is adjacent to an 8-story shopping mall.

voyage.name: New Asia Hotel Jin Jiang
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at ¥228+
voyage.content: Offers 328 guestrooms, all of which have air-conditioning, satellite TV with in-room movies, and high-speed Internet. Some of its amenities include sauna, health/fitness center, and massage service.

voyage.name: South China Harbour View Hotel
voyage.content: Close to Waibaidu Bridge, on the Huangpu River.

voyage.name: Shanghai Yinbo Hotel
voyage.content: Three-star hotel near Shanghai’s city conveniences and popular landmarks. It offers cozy accommodation and friendly service.

voyage.name: Swan Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. All rooms are air-conditioned and feature high-speed Internet access, cable TV, safe, and IDD telephone. It also houses conference rooms that can accommodate up to 100 persons, and nine restaurants.

voyage.name: Grand Mercure Baolong Hotel Shanghai
voyage.content: Close to major shopping areas, points of interest and cultural centres, including local attractions such as Lu Xun Park, historic Duolun Rd and Fudan University.
